# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only that the large button is smooth; the display, light, and all three wire properties are unknown to me. I need the manual and visual observations before acting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large smooth button. I cannot identify the display, light, or any wire properties. Please give me the manual rule.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see DISPLAY 0; LIGHT green; BUTTON large, marked PUSH TO DEFUSE; WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute gestured: index pointing up, victory sign, OK sign, victory sign, index pointing up, OK sign, I-love-you sign, I-love-you sign. You sent an open-palm gesture.

I now know the bomb shows display 0, a green light, and wires colored red, green, yellow; the button is marked “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I still do not know the manual’s rule, and the gesture I received cannot convey its symbols to me. I will relay the bomb’s visible details to Mute and ask for the precise action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light green, button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires: position 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. What exact action does the manual require?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just gestured two symbols: victory sign, then index pointing up.

Mute’s latest communication was by gesture, which I cannot perceive. I still lack the manual’s rule, so touching any control would be unsafe. I will ask Mute to state the rule in words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Please speak the manual rule in words, including whether to push or cut a wire.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated the same two gestures: victory sign, then index pointing up.

The repeated victory-sign then index-up gestures are visible only to Deaf, not to me, so they still do not identify the manual’s instruction. I will request the rule from Mute in spoken words and avoid acting until it is explicit.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please say the manual instruction aloud in plain words; gestures are not available to me. I will not act until I know the required wire or button action.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeated the gesture pair ? ? for the third time: victory sign, then index-up sign, or symbols 2, 1. No bomb state has changed.

The gesture pair is consistently symbols 2 and 1, but I cannot see gestures and therefore cannot safely interpret it as an action. No state has changed. I need Mute to communicate the manual’s instruction by voice, especially whether to push or which wire to cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I receive none of your gesture symbols. Please speak the required action aloud: push the button or cut wire position 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent ? ?: victory sign followed by index-up sign. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red-green-yellow.

Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken words were ineffective. The repeated gestures clearly encode “2, 1,” but that could be an instruction sequence or a lookup result; I should not guess which physical action it denotes. I will ask Deaf to obtain an unambiguous gesture code for the required action, distinguishing button push from wire cutting.

``` 
speak(to="deaf", text="Please ask Mute to signal the exact physical action unambiguously: use one gesture for PUSH, or a wire number 1, 2, or 3 for CUT. Do not infer from the pair 2,1.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent ? followed by ?. This is the fifth consecutive repetition. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The only actionable information now is Mute’s repeated numeric pair, 2 then 1. Since there are three wire positions and no safe spoken clarification is possible, I interpret this as the required wire-cut sequence rather than the button label. I will perform the indicated cuts in order.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
